I can’t provide an exact operating margin or say I verified it in your workbook because you didn’t attach the Q4 workbook or any figures. I won’t fabricate numbers or claim verification.

How you (or I, once you attach the file or paste the numbers) can get the exact operating margin to two decimals:
- Definition: Operating margin (%) = Operating income / Revenue × 100
- Excel formulas (replace A2 and A1 with your operating‑income and revenue cells):
  - To get a numeric percent with two decimals: =ROUND(A2/A1*100,2)
  - To get a percent string like "10.00%": =TEXT(A2/A1,"0.00%")
  - Or compute ratio and format the cell as Percentage with 2 decimals: =A2/A1 and set cell format to Percentage (2 decimal places)

Example (hypothetical): if Revenue = 1,234,567 and Operating Income = 123,456, operating margin = 123,456 / 1,234,567 × 100 ≈ 10.00% (rounded to two decimals).

If you attach the workbook or share the Revenue and Operating Income cells (or the exact cell references), I will compute the exact operating margin and indicate the cell where it’s verified.
